entities.name: Transient soap pH effect
observations: Human evidence indicates alkaline soap acutely raises skin-surface pH; an infant study reported a +0.45 pH-unit rise 10 minutes after pH 9.5 soap, with no recovery measurement.
Reviews report post-wash surface pH generally returns toward physiologic values over several hours; permanent alteration of intrinsic pH maintenance has not been demonstrated in human studies.

Repeated cleansing can remove surface lipids and burden the barrier; acidic pH supports barrier lipid processing and antimicrobial defense, but direct soap trials measuring persistent pH-mechanism changes are lacking.
